source_refs.note: Exercise 5.2, Question 4 (book p. 158); answer key PDF 306

blocks.prompt: 4 The angle from the line \(ax - y + 2 = 0\) to the line \(x + y - 4 = 0\) is \(30^\circ\). Find the value of \(a\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh ulta sawal hai: angle maloom hai aur ek line ke slope mein unknown \(a\) chhupa hua hai.
Dono slopes likhenge, Theorem 7 mein \(\tan 30^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) rakhenge, aur jo equation banegi use \(a\) ke liye hal karenge.
Order ahem hai: pehli line 'from' hai, is ka slope \(m_1\).
Plan: slopes, formula = \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), cross-multiply, \(a\) nikaalna, rationalise.
Yahan answer key do values deti hai, lekin hum dekhenge ke 'from ... to' ki shart sirf ek value poori karti hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\ell_1: ax - y + 2 = 0\), \(\ell_2: x + y - 4 = 0\), aur \(\ell_1\) se \(\ell_2\) tak angle \(\theta = 30^\circ\).
Maloom karna: \(a\).
Tareeqa: slopes \(-\frac{a}{b}\) se, Theorem 7, phir \(a\) ki linear equation hal karna.

Slopes nikalein
\[m_1 = -\dfrac{a}{-1} = a\]
\[m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{1} = -1\]
Kyun: \(\ell_1\) mein \(y\) ka coefficient \(-1\) hai, is liye slope seedha \(a\) ban gaya. Yani \(a\) hi pehli line ka slope hai, aur isi ko humein dhoondna hai.

Theorem 7 lagayein
\[\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{-1 - a}{1 + a(-1)}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{-1 - a}{1 - a}\]
Kyun: \(m_2 = -1\) pehle aata hai, aur \(\tan 30^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) yaad hona chahiye.

Cross-multiply kar ke \(a\) ikattha karein
\[1 - a = \sqrt{3}(-1 - a)\]
\[1 - a = -\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{3}a\]
\[\sqrt{3}a - a = -\sqrt{3} - 1\]
\[a(\sqrt{3} - 1) = -(\sqrt{3} + 1)\]
Kyun: \(a\) wale terms ek taraf aur numbers doosri taraf; phir \(a\) ko common nikala.
Dhyan dein: side badalne par sign badalta hai; \(-\sqrt{3}a\) left par aa kar \(+\sqrt{3}a\) bana.

Hal karein aur rationalise karein
\[a = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}\]
\[= -\dfrac{(\sqrt{3} + 1)^2}{3 - 1}\]
\[= -\dfrac{4 + 2\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[a = -2 - \sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: denominator se root hatane ke liye upar neeche \(\sqrt{3} + 1\) se multiply kiya; neeche \((\sqrt{3})^2 - 1^2 = 2\), upar \((\sqrt{3} + 1)^2 = 3 + 2\sqrt{3} + 1\).

Tasdeeq:
\(a \approx -3.732\) rakhein:
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-1 + 3.732}{1 + 3.732}\]
\[= \dfrac{2.732}{4.732} \approx 0.5774 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \;\checkmark\]
yani \(\theta = 30^\circ\), bilkul jaisa sawal ne kaha.
Khulasa: ulte sawal mein bhi wohi formula hai; bas unknown slope ke andar hai aur aakhir mein ek seedhi si linear equation hal karni parti hai. Rationalise karna mat bhooliye, kyunke jawab saaf shakal mein likhna chahiye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Answer key do values deti hai, \(-2 + \sqrt{3}\) aur \(-2 - \sqrt{3}\). Lekin sirf \(a = -2 - \sqrt{3}\) se \(ax - y + 2 = 0\) se \(x + y - 4 = 0\) tak ka angle \(30^\circ\) banta hai.
\(a = -2 + \sqrt{3}\) rakhein to \(\tan\theta = \frac{-1 - a}{1 - a} = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{3 - \sqrt{3}} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), yani pehli line se doosri tak angle \(150^\circ\) hai. Yeh value sirf tab sahi hoti jab sawal 'lines ke darmiyan acute angle 30 degree' kehta, direction ke beghair.
